protocol_checks.vulnerability_mechanism: Confirmed both advisory mechanisms: html_to_markdown routes request['url'] to requests.get(url) without URL or destination validation or a timeout, enabling SSRF; qrcode fetches an attacker-selected remote image with verify=False, disabling TLS certificate validation.
protocol_checks.atomic_bic: Confirmed 2be1d7a0cde74703e15e2afd70c4205d9a4c3844 as the atomic first write of the html_to_markdown SSRF path. The separate qrcode TLS flaw is first written by 925e2e8089a0676b4bad2be4bafda9897346b906; the primary record explicitly distinguishes this secondary advisory surface.
protocol_checks.immediate_parent_absence: Confirmed: 2be1d7a0 has sole parent c00349e1984ee7b00b88eb36e382f9a5c98cd94e, whose tree has no html_to_markdown.py. The sole parent of 925e2e80 has qrcode.py but no requests-based remote fetch or verify=False.
protocol_checks.squash_member_decomposition: Confirmed no substitution by a move, refactor, revert, merge, or later carrier: 2be1d7a0 is a single-parent new-file commit and the smallest surviving public first-write object. The secondary 925e2e80 commit is also single-parent, and its diff itself first adds the remote-fetch code and verify=False; no finer member object is present in the available history.
protocol_checks.affected_fixed_release_membership: Confirmed by tag ancestry and tag-tree inspection: v3.0.7 contains both BICs, still has unvalidated requests.get(url), still has verify=False, and excludes 52cda9ca. v3.0.8 contains 52cda9ca and both remediations. Thus the repository history contradicts the CVE text claiming fixed in 3.0.7, exactly as the primary record reports. Later IPv4-mapped-IPv6 hardening first appears in v3.0.9.
protocol_checks.direct_fix_or_unpatched: Confirmed 52cda9caa003cafe87e14ae3721db5e16f6f111a as the direct remediation: it adds URL scheme/IP/DNS checks and timeout=10 to html_to_markdown and removes verify=False from qrcode. Advisory-linked 01a522f2772fc31eeed379ccf23750c8a3d401db is only a whitespace-format follow-up. The primary also correctly records later SSRF bypass hardening rather than hiding it.
protocol_checks.bic_only_ai_attribution: Confirmed NOT_AI from the BIC objects only: 2be1d7a0 is authored and committed by mokaddem <sami.mokaddem@circl.lu> and has no AI/co-author/bot trailer or identity; the secondary 925e2e80 object is authored and committed by Nassima <nassima.aidi@univ-rouen.fr> and likewise has no trailer. findings: The primary record reconstructs the complete source-to-sink and remediation lifecycle and correctly separates the advisory's SSRF and TLS-validation mechanisms.
